### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via enforceApiExposure (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **39** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 67b669e6890a20f443c0aa9309d6b6238913718a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `19b8bbf86132b0c20fe3054fabbd383775fc6d32` — the merge of head `2261c253ec75c2412914df2c11a998a9ec9713c6` into base `67b669e6890a20f443c0aa9309d6b6238913718a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 19b8bbf86132b0c20fe3054fabbd383775fc6d32 && git checkout 19b8bbf86132b0c20fe3054fabbd383775fc6d32
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 67b669e6890a20f443c0aa9309d6b6238913718a 2261c253ec75c2412914df2c11a998a9ec9713c6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 67b669e6890a20f443c0aa9309d6b6238913718a && git merge --no-ff 2261c253ec75c2412914df2c11a998a9ec9713c6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 67b669e6890a20f443c0aa9309d6b6238913718a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 67b669e6890a20f443c0aa9309d6b6238913718a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2261c253ec75c2412914df2c11a998a9ec9713c6`
Local-runs: none

Inputs, and nothing else: card #22777 (body; the claim 6107453288; the os-dev-report 6108171450), the family precedent (PR #22768's contract reviews 6106147584 and 6107185299, and the seat's ACCEPT 6107195645 on #22737), PR #22820 (body; its 9-file list; the net diff from merge-base `c11b75870a` to the head: 9 files, +348/−46, byte-matching the file list), `git show ec7c7e0637:packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` against the head's `packages/core/src/utils/relation-condition-sites.ts` and `protocol.ts` (object-store reads in the shared checkout: no checkout, no build, no test, no gate), `origin/main` at `b7cd1af9df` through `git merge-tree --write-tree`, and the head's check-runs, read 2026-10-11T10:58Z: 33 check-runs, 23 concluded `success` (Auto Label, Build Core, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate and its three shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Flag docs affected, Governed Surface Queue Guard, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Temporal Conformance, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · consumer gates / debt ledger / source gates / workspace, TypeScript Type Check, filter), 3 `skipped` by their own triggers (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke), and 7 IN PROGRESS (Lint and Repo Gates; Test Core 1/6 through 6/6; the bare `Test Core` context not yet posted). Judged on what has concluded; see ③. Security card: classes, positions and functions only.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The moved walk.** `relationConditionSites` at the head (`packages/core/src/utils/relation-condition-sites.ts`) against the one `ec7c7e0637` held module-private in `protocol.ts` (lines 4487–4516 there): the function body is identical line for line under `diff -w`. What differs is the indentation (the data door's four spaces, core's two), the `export`, the inline return type replaced by the new exported interface `RelationConditionSite` (the same three members: `field`, `target`, `condition`), the docblock's #22777 paragraph, and the three-line private `isPlainRecord` carried into the module (`protocol.ts` keeps its own, which has other callers). "Moved unchanged" is right for the logic and the accept set; not byte-for-byte, and the changeset claims the logic, not the bytes. **Right.**
2. **The data door still calls it at every position it did, and `refuseUnservedRelationTarget` is untouched.** Between `ec7c7e0637` and the head the net diff of `protocol.ts` inside this PR is two hunks: the `@objectstack/core` import line gains `relationConditionSites`, and the private function is deleted. The 136-line region holding `assertNoInternalFieldEvaluated`, `refuseInternalInFilter` (the one textual call site of the walk, reached for `where`, the `filter` alias, each `aggregations[i].filter`, and each expand entry's own `where` at every level through `refuseInternalInExpand`) and `refuseUnservedRelationTarget` is byte-identical at the two shas (`diff` empty). A third hunk between those shas (near line 16669) is `main`'s own drift, outside this PR's net diff. The dev's ablation B (the walk mutated on core's `dist`, the data door's own pin going red) is the measurement that the door now runs the moved walk; this record judges the wiring, which it confirms. **Right.**
3. **One decision, operation `list`, before any engine read, on both verbs.** `enforceRelationTargetExposure` (`stdio-data-bridge.ts`, the function after `enforceApiExposure`) walks `opts.where` with the shared walk against the addressed object's field map and calls `enforceApiExposure(metadataService, site.target, GATED_ACTIONS.query, context, position)` for each site, the position spelled `where.FIELD`. `GATED_ACTIONS.query` is `'query'` and `DATA_ACTION_TO_API_OPERATION.query` is `'list'` (`@objectstack/spec/data`), the operation `refuseUnservedRelationTarget` asks (`RELATION_CONDITION_TARGET_OPERATION`), for the reason the precedent gave: the engine's lowering reads the target as the caller with the condition as the whole predicate (`ObjectQL.lowerRelationConditions` runs `this.find` on the target), the target's own list read. The gate asked is the bridge's pre-existing #8083 gate, the one an addressed object gets; no new rule. On the face: `enforceApiExposure` asks `resolveEffectiveApiMethods` and `isApiOperationAllowed` directly after its own `apiEnabled === false` branch, in the order `apiExposureDenialReason` composes those same two functions; the data door asks the composed face. One decision, two faces; named because the census pin's D2 leg reads only the composed face (①.8). Ordering: in `query()` the call sits after the addressed object's gate and before `storedMetadataBodyRefusal`, `storedMetadataHashRefusal` and `engine.find`; in `aggregate` after the addressed gate (`GATED_ACTIONS.aggregate`) and before the body and hash refusals and `engine.aggregate`. No engine read precedes it on either verb (the metadata service, not the engine, is read for the field map). Placing it ahead of the #21207 refusals only decides which refusal wins when both apply; both refuse before the engine. **Right.**
4. **Positions walked: `where` only, and that is every filter position this door carries.** `McpDataBridge.query` takes `where`, `fields`, `limit`, `offset`, `orderBy`; `aggregate` takes `where`, `groupBy`, `aggregations`, `timezone`. The stdio bridge is engine-only and carries no `filter` alias and no `expand` (the HTTP bridge's extras, as the file header records). `aggregations[i].filter`, verified at the head: the `aggregate_records` tool's aggregation item schema declares `function`, `field`, `alias` and nothing else; `strictToolInput` applies `.strict()` to the top-level object only, so an unknown nested key is dropped by zod's default rather than refused, and never reaches the bridge. At the bridge's own interface the engine's `EngineAggregateOptions['aggregations']` type does admit a `filter`, and there the engine refuses a nested-relation condition: `relation-filter-lowering.ts`'s ruling, "An aggregation's own `filter` and `having` keep the no-operator-object refusal: the engine evaluates both itself, over rows it already holds". Refused, not lowered, no target read. Deviation (c) verifies. The data door's AST-carrier parse (`isFilterAST`) has no input here: the tool admits a plain-object `where` only. **Right.**
5. **One hop.** The engine's `admitRelationCondition` refuses a site beneath a site (`second-level`, and the `dotted-key` spelling) with `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 before `lowerRelationConditions` reads anything; the data door recurses deeper only for its internal-field judgement. One level of asking covers every site the engine will run. Deviation (d) verifies. **Right.**
6. **The `isSystem` bypass the reused gate keeps.** `enforceApiExposure` returns at once for `context.isSystem` (#8083, matching `callData`'s first condition); #22737's `refuseUnservedRelationTarget` takes no caller and refuses a system context too. Reachability from this door, read at the head: the bridge's only context source is `deps.resolvePrincipal`, wired once in `plugin.ts` to `resolveStdioExecutionContext`, which returns `assembleExecutionContext` over the resolved API-key authz; the assembler's `entryFields` emits `isSystem: false` as a literal (`assemble-execution-context.ts:318`) with no input that can flip it, and `resolvePrincipal` throws when the assembler returns `undefined`. The `isSystem: true` contexts inside `resolveAuthzContext` are its own internal lookups, not the returned principal. `plugin-execution-context.test.ts` already pins `context.isSystem === false` on the stdio chain. So no caller of this door reaches the bypass, and every reachable caller gets #22737's verdict. The divergence exists in the function (an in-package host injecting a system principal would bypass) and is unreachable at the head; neither `createStdioDataBridge` nor `enforceApiExposure` is published from `@objectstack/mcp`'s index. **Right as measured; named.** The flat-shape read (`def.enable`, else `def`) is the other inherited difference from the door: the bridge can refuse a legacy flat definition the door would serve, stricter, #8083's, not this class.
7. **Tool surface.** `query_records` and `aggregate_records` both end in `catch (err) { return errorResult(messageOf(err)); }`, the same flattening an addressed-object refusal gets; the thrown `McpExposureError` carries `code`, `status` and `allowedOperations`, and the message names the target, the position (`where.FIELD`) and the remedy in the data door's words (the `consequence` suffix added to both branches of `enforceApiExposure`). The pin's tool leg holds `isError` and both names over an in-memory MCP pair. Disclosure judged as the precedent did: the lookup's declared target is in the source's `describe_object` answer already, and the 405 set is what the target answers when addressed. **Right.**
8. **The census pin.** The new row classifies `packages/core/src/utils/relation-condition-sites.ts` `not-a-served-read` (finds sites, reads no record), naming both callers in its reason. Applying the pin's own discriminator to the diff: the new file calls `referenceTargetOf` on a code line, so an unclassified head would red test 1 and the row is owed; `protocol.ts` still calls the arbiter at its expand sites, so its `decided` row does not go stale; the decided list stays exact at six; `stdio-data-bridge.ts` calls neither the arbiter nor either face of the decision, so the discriminator does not see it, as the dev says. Not `decided`, for two structural reasons the dev's one covers: a CALLERS key is one file with one decision, and the walk file serves two doors; and a `decided` row for the bridge would fail the D2 leg's letter, which reads `apiExposureDenialReason` / `canServeApiOperation` and not the two constituents the bridge's #8083 gate asks (①.3), and converting that gate to the composed face would be a change to the gate "it already applies", outside the card's direction. Soundness: a later read that resolves its target through `referenceTargetOf` still turns the pin red, unchanged; a later door that reaches the engine's lowering without the data door and without the arbiter was invisible before this PR (the bridge itself was, which is the card's premise) and stays invisible after it, so publishing the walk opens no blind spot the pin did not already have, and the header now names the class instead of discovering it later. Held rather than named: the bridge's ask is held by `stdio-data-bridge.relation-condition-target-exposure.test.ts`, 24 refusal cells (four target shapes: API-disabled, create-only, get-only, deny-all; direct, under `$or`, under `$not`; `query` and `aggregate`), each asserting `code`, `status`, `allowedOperations` on 405, the target and the position in the message, and that neither `engine.find` nor `engine.aggregate` was called. The get-only cell is what reds a switch of the operation to `get`; the `aggregate` cells red a dropped second call. Controls hold a list-only target, an open target, an id comparand and an operator bag reaching the engine with `where` by reference. The dev's ablation A (25 red / 2 green) is the measurement; not re-run here. The walk's own pin (`relation-condition-sites.test.ts`) holds the top level, each combinator, the implicit `user` target and the no-field-map stand-down. The new row's prose names `enforceRelationTargetExposure` without a wiring check; that is the header's "named, not held" and the mcp pin is the hold. **Right.**
9. **Public surface.** `@objectstack/core` gains `relationConditionSites` and the interface `RelationConditionSite` via `export *` from `index.ts`, beside the sibling door helpers (`object-not-found`, `record-not-found`); the module imports `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES` and `referenceTargetOf` from `@objectstack/spec/data`, a dependency core already declares and exercises (`import-field-meta.ts` is a classified arbiter caller). `@objectstack/mcp`: `enforceApiExposure`'s optional fifth parameter is in-package (not exported from `index.ts`), so the package's published change is the accept set at the stdio tool surface only. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: the walk leaves its `dist` and is imported; no exported member moves. `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/types` untouched, as claimed. **Right.**
10. **Reach.** Stated on a real stack at base `23419bafb7` over the #22661 fixture, administrator and member, both tools, through the plugin's own principal chain over an in-memory MCP pair; the stdio byte transport and the process boundary not exercised, the bound #22737's dev stated when it found this door. **Right; the bound is named.**

### ② Semver level

- **`.changeset/22777-mcp-stdio-relation-condition-target-exposure.md`: `@objectstack/mcp` `minor`**, `!` summary, `**BREAKING**` banner, FROM (both tools judged the addressed object only) → TO (each condition's related object asked the addressed gate for `list`, refused with the existing pair), a migration paragraph, the PR's `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` line, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` in an HTML comment. **Right**: a narrowing is breaking and the launch window ships breaking as `minor` (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`); `Check Changeset`, which runs that gate and `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` against the merge base (`pr-automation.yml` lines 979–980 and 1130), concluded `success` on this head. The marker's honesty, judged by the checker's own header rather than by its silence: the category is refused "when the changeset's own body carries a migration prescription" in the sense of "instructions for rewriting a consumer's code", an old-to-new pair, a rename or a removal, the thing a ledger entry would drive `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite. This body moves no spec key, spelling, export or stored shape; its `**Migration.**` sentence names a runtime request the caller can already write and an opt-in (`list` on the related object's `enable.apiMethods`) that already exists; and the marker argues that in writing and closes the other four categories on facts (published; no id named; no exported declaration removed or narrowed), which is what the header's #8277 paragraph asks of an author relying on this category. The imperative-sentence residue the header calls "deliberately out of reach" is where this body sits, and the marker does not rest on it. Same shape as #22737's changeset, which both precedent records and the ACCEPT held right. **Honest.**
- **`.changeset/22777-core-relation-condition-sites.md`: `@objectstack/core` `minor`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `patch`, one non-breaking changeset.** **Right**: one additive export (the `yes` of the PR's line) is the floor for `minor`; metadata-protocol ships a different `dist` (the function replaced by an import) with no behaviour change, and `patch` is the honest floor for a released package whose bytes move. The core export's name, module and exported type are the right published surface (①.9): the name the data door already used and the card named, the type naming what the inline type carried, the module where core keeps the helpers both doors share.
- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`** on line 2 of the PR body and in the breaking changeset. **Right value, right arm**: the value answers whether the card widens an accept set or the public surface (`clause2-line.mjs`), and core's export does; the arm names the mcp narrowing, which is the breaking fact; the ADR-0087 checker's own self-test names this exact spelling as "a diff that widens AND narrows". Deviation (i) is answered.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviations (a)–(i).** (a) Base `23419bafb7`; `main` `c11b75870a` merged as the head. `origin/main` is now `b7cd1af9df`, five commits past the merge base (#22815, #22814, #22811, #22816, #22785, landed 2026-10-11T09:38Z to 2026-10-11T10:17Z); none touches the 9 paths (empty intersection), and `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the head onto `b7cd1af9df` merges clean (object-store read). In the branch's dependency directories the drift is #22785's `import-field-meta.ts` (a classified arbiter caller, still classified) and `metadata-activation-store.ts`; nothing near the walk, the bridge or the pin's rows. #22816 rewrote `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (a console-only leg); the head's `Check Changeset` run started 2026-10-11T10:39Z, after that landed, on the merge ref against then-current `main`, so the gate as it stands on `main` has judged these changesets. No re-merge is owed by this record; the queue builds against then-current `main`. (b) 394 changed lines against the dispatch's suggested 300: `Check PR Size` concluded `success` (it is configured not to fail on size); the composition is source +124/−45 (net +79: +48/−3 mcp, +69 core walk offset by −42/+1 `protocol.ts`, +6 index), two new pins (+136, +32), the census header and row (+15/−1) and two changesets (+41). The excess is pins and the move, not scope. **Right.** (c) `where` only: ①.4. (d) One hop: ①.5. (e) `isSystem`: ①.6. (f) Changesets: ②. (g) Zero label writes: right, the dispatch named none and changesets exist. (h) **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally (exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET): answered by CI.** The step `Every published require entry point actually loads` (`pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`) lives in `ci.yml`'s `Build Core` job, after the full build, for exactly the reason the dev hit (it needs every `dist`); `Build Core` concluded `success` on this head at 2026-10-11T10:45:43Z. That is the gate verdict; the dev's narrowed `require()` probe is superseded, and was honestly labelled. (i) The PR body's line 2: ②.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1, the MCP HTTP door's `callData` fallback: escalated.** Read at the head: `callData`'s query arm (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`, lines 349–393) prefers `protocol.findData` (the data door #22737 decided) and, when no protocol service resolves, hands a key-filtered bag including `where` to `ql.find` after judging only the addressed object (`checkApiExposure`, line 43). The file's own comments say that branch runs "on an assembly where the protocol plugin is absent", so it is a composition the code anticipates, not a hypothetical. That is this card's class at a third position, in `packages/runtime`, outside this claim's surface; the dev bounded it correctly ("not measured here") and it does not hold this PR. Carrier: none is not enough for a same-class door in a security family: the seat should either measure that composition or file it as a census row on #22661 beside row 8.
- **Out-of-scope finding 2, the tool surface answers text only: answered.** `errorResultFromThrown` (#15942) exists in the same file for the confirmation gate; the two data tools flatten every bridge refusal, addressed or relation, through `errorResult(messageOf(err))` since #8083. Pre-existing, identical for both refusal positions, and the pin's tool leg holds the text that names the target and the position. A machine-readable envelope at the tool would be a widening for both positions together, its own card if wanted; not this class and not a hold.
- **Check-runs at this read: 7 in progress.** `Lint and Repo Gates` (eslint over the 7 changed `.ts` files, the changeset-family self-tests and the repo gates) and `Test Core` shards 1/6 through 6/6 (which carry the new mcp pin, the walk's pin, the census pin in core's `repo` project and metadata-protocol's relation-condition pin) had not concluded; the bare `Test Core` context was not yet posted. This record judges the diff, the card and the 26 concluded runs; the dev's local numbers (mcp 36 files / 417; core `local` 2364 and `repo` 55; metadata-protocol 28129; dogfood 34/34; 66 of 67 gate commands at exit 0) are the dev's measurements and were not re-run here. Every check green is the queue's own condition and is not waived by this verdict; a red among the seven produces a new head, which owes its own record.
- **Landing facts for the owning seat.** Draft, auto-merge unarmed, `mergeable_state: blocked` (checks pending), head repo equals base repo. None of the 9 paths hits a `GOVERNED_SURFACES` row; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded `success`. The `packages/mcp` path is `domain:cli`, declared on #6024 per the claim. This record is the Clause-② contract-tier review the narrowing owes before the queue, not a Tier S landing record.
